newsitem.title: USA: Berkshire Hathaway profits jump on GEICO boost.
newsitem.headline: Berkshire Hathaway profits jump on GEICO boost.

text.p: Berkshire Hathaway Inc., the diversified holding company headed by investor Warren Buffett, Monday reported higher third-quarter earnings, boosted by the performance of GEICO Corp.
Berkshire's profits rose to $264 million, or $218 a share, in the quarter ended Sept. 30, from $194.5 million, or $163 a share, in the year-ago period.
The company's operating earnings rose to $201.4 million from $151.3 million.
On Jan. 2, Berkshire completed the acquisition of about 49 percent of GEICO's common stock, giving it control of the insurance company.

"Though we are pleased that our gain in per-share book value during the first nine months of 1996 outpaced the gain of the S&P 500, the real news at Berkshire this year is the exceptional performance of GEICO," Buffett said in a statement.
"There has been a substantial acceleration in the growth of voluntary auto business accompanied by outstanding underwriting profitability. We expect continued growth in new business."
Berkshire's class A stock was unchanged at $32,900 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday. Its class B stock fell $1 to $1,093, also on the NYSE.
